edge.title: Muon lr 0.025→0.035 (from #10); schedule 3350, report at 3325
edge.summary: Raises Muon lr from 0.025 to 0.035 at the same wd=0.025, copying NorMuon #10's lr/wd (lr·wd 6.25e-4 → 8.75e-4 per step at peak). The schedule now spans 3350 steps but the result is read at step 3325, 25 steps before the LR reaches zero (≈1.1% of peak), following #8; validation runs every 25 steps in the last 10% so the stop step can be fixed in advance for all seeds. The README's pairwise test finds these Muon hparams significantly better than #6's.

changes.label: Muon lr 0.025 → 0.035
changes.detail: optimizer2 = Muon(lr=0.035, weight_decay=0.025): the lr/wd pair of NorMuon record #10 applied to plain Muon.

changes.label: Early stop 25 steps before end
changes.detail: train_steps 3375 → 3350 defines the LR schedule, but the claimed result is the val loss at step 3325, inside the final cooldown (as in #8).

changes.label: Validation every 25 steps in last 10%
changes.detail: val_step_freq = 125 if step/train_steps < 0.9 else 25, so val is logged every 25 steps from step 3025 on. Eval-only, but it is what makes the 3325 readout possible.

changes.label: Minor cleanups
changes.detail: The data loader calls dist.get_world_size()/get_rank() inline and the init loop aliases w = p.data. No behavioral effect.

edge.parent_check: Consistent (declared). This script equals train_gpt_simple.py at git 73ba757 (2026-05-03): the #6 baseline plus the tail-validation, lr and steps edits. Influences: #10 (lr=0.035, wd=0.025) and #8 (25-step early stop).
edge.noise: Data-loader inlining of world_size/rank and the w = p.data alias.

techniques.note: lr 0.035, wd 0.025, mu 0.95 Nesterov, NS 12 iters (2,-1.5,0.5)
claimed at 3325 of 3350 scheduled (lr ≈ 1.1% of peak)
proj weights zero (incl. LM head); all biases zero

hparams.init.hidden_std: normal, std 0.33**0.5 / fan_in**0.5 ≈ 0.0207 (q, k, v, mlp.fc)
hparams.init.proj: zero (attn.proj, mlp.proj and LM head weights)

mechanisms.name: Early stop inside the cooldown
mechanisms.explain: The LR schedule is defined over train_steps=3350, but the record reports the val loss at a fixed earlier step (3325) that is the same for every seed, using the 25-step validation grid of the last 10%. This gives up the last ~1% of the linear decay in exchange for fewer counted steps; per the rules the stop point is chosen once for all runs, not per run.

caveats: n=20, mean 3.2790 at 3325: (3.28 − 3.27905)·√20 ≈ 0.0043, just above the 0.004 bar. The README uses this record to calibrate the step–loss trade-off: 200 fewer steps raise the mean to 3.2881 (≈0.0045 per 100 steps), and its pairwise test vs #6 gives 0.00648 ≥ 0.004.
